---
title: "Portfolio Project 3"
subtitle: "Incorporating Interactivity"
---

# Overview

For your third portfolio project, you'll apply what you've learned about interactivity and revisit a previous portfolio project. (If you'd prefer to revisit a homework problem, in-class activity, etc. that is also OK!) 

Your task is to choose one of the previous portfolio projects that you've done, and add interactivity to it! 

Some tools you might consider: 

  - plotly
  - leaflet
  - DataTable
  - Shiny
  
You should think carefully about how your chosen interactive components can *add* to the static version of your previous project, and include a 1 paragraph summary of why you chose the interactivity that you did. I want to see that you can implement the technical tools that we've covered, but also that you know how to deploy them effectively. 

# Submission

Your submission will be a github repo **and** your published product. This should be either a knitted .html file that has been published to the web, or a shiny app hosted on shinyapps.io. 

*Please test your published version before submitting!* 

# Rubric

A **successful** project will:

- [ ] Include all necessary components pushed to GitHub and linked to gradescope
- [ ] Demonstrate a history of work in progress and revision through your git commit history
- [ ] The .qmd (or .R) has all necessary and no unnecessary code
- [ ] The output file is .html and I can render it. 
- [ ] There are at least two interactive components (a plotly counts as one; each distinct type of shiny input counts as one)
- [ ] The README file includes (1) a link to your published report (2) an explanation of how to navigate your repo, (3) a paragraph explaining the interactivity that you've added and why it is an improvement over the original static version
- [ ] Meet minimum submission quality standards
    -   [ ] Very few grammatical mistakes, spelling mistakes, or typos
    -   [ ] Informative title for your report is included
    -   [ ] Any graphs are readable with appropriate titles and labels
    -   [ ] The rendered document does not contain any unnecessary content (package loading messages, warnings, etc.)

An **excellent** project will meet all of the requirements for a successful project, plus

- [ ] Include a published URL
    - [ ] The shiny app has at least two types of interactivity included, and the README includes a thoughtful discussion of why the interactivity helps 
    - I recommend using [posit connect cloud](https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/posit-connect-cloud.html#publish-command) but you could also consider [github pages](https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages.html). If you have a personal website you want to publish to, that's great too! Please include a URL in your README.md file so I can find your report when grading
    -   There are lots of reasons you might not want the world to know that you are enrolled in this class, and this is one of your rights under FERPA. If you're not comfortable including your name, you don't have to! Your public document can be authored by "Student" (which has a [history](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.351.6280.1406) of being used in statistics).
- [ ] High degree of technical
    - [ ] Is a shiny app with at least two interactive components
    - [ ] If not shiny, goes substantially beyond the plotly/leaflet/DT that we covered in class
- [ ] Meet high submission quality standards
    - [ ] No grammatical mistakes, spelling mistakes, or typos
    - [ ] Graphs have been customized (theme, color palette, scales, etc.) 

# Can I work with someone? 

Yes! You can work individually or with a partner for this portfolio project. If you work with a partner, please let me know by the end of the day on Monday Week 9. (Keeping in mind that you cannot work with the same person on more than 2 projects) 

# Are revisions allowed on this project? 

The project is due Friday of Week 9, and I cannot accept any coursework except for the final project past the last day of class due to College policy. I cannot guarantee that I will have this graded in time for you to revise, but I will grade and release grades in the order they were submitted, so you are more likely to have time to revise if you submit early.
